turns.content: It's 2am and I'm still at the office. Not working — just sitting. The bridge round officially died on Tuesday. Rohit and Sneha put in their papers this week, which honestly, smart. Four months of runway if I stop taking salary, which I already have. I built this thing for five years.

That sounds tough. Five years is a huge investment, and to see it not working out... it's natural to feel stuck. You're not alone in feeling this way. Did you expect it to go down like this, or is it a surprise?

The worst part is the performance. Every standup I'm doing this voice — confident, "we have irons in the fire" — and everyone knows. My co-founder knows. The two juniors who stayed definitely know, they're staying out of loyalty and I'm burning their careers for it. At home I do a different voice. I'm so tired of my own voices, man.

It's like you're living two separate lives, and both are taking a toll on you. Putting on a brave face at work while feeling like you're failing, and then having to deal with the weight of it all at home. That can't be easy. And on top of that, feeling responsible for the juniors' careers... that's a heavy burden. Do you feel like you're being honest with anyone right now?

Please don't give me ideas. I know all the ideas. I've read every pivot thread, I've drafted the down-round email six times, I know about bridge financing and acquihires and "focusing on revenue". I know. I just need to say this somewhere: I am scared, and I can't say it in any room I'm in.

Sometimes just saying it out loud can be a relief. You're scared, and that's okay. It's okay to admit it, even if it's just to someone who's not in any of your rooms. I'm here, and you can say it. You've put in the work, and now you're facing the uncertainty. It's normal to feel scared. It feels like a lot is riding on what's next.

Is it over? Like actually — you can be honest. Five years. My dad still tells people I have a "computer business". Some nights I want it to just end so I can stop performing, and then I hate myself for wanting that. Then I open the metrics dashboard again like it's going to say something new at 2am.

It feels like you're stuck in limbo. Part of you wants to move on, but another part is holding on, hoping something will change. Checking the metrics dashboard at 2 am is like hoping for a miracle. It's hard to let go when you've invested so much. Your dad still thinking you're running a successful "computer business" adds to the pressure. You're caught between wanting to be done with it all and holding on to the hope that things will turn around.
